title: Traffic Source & AOV Analysis
text:
For our IBM 6540 (Applied Machine Learning for Marketing) group project, our five-person team analyzed a 60,000-row Shopify sales dataset. I owned RO1: traffic source and average order value (AOV) and wrote the conclusion slides.
Finding: No statistically significant overall difference in AOV between channels, but meaningful channel × category interaction effects. Some channels performed better for specific product categories.
Tools: R, recipes, rsample, glmnet, Quarto revealjs

title: Listings in Quarto
text:
A listing is a Quarto feature that automatically builds a gallery, list, or table from a set of pages. Instead of hand-coding a “Projects” page and updating it every time you finish something, you drop a new .qmd file into a folder and Quarto adds it to the listing on the next render.
Each item pulls its title, date, description, image, and categories from that page’s YAML header.

title: Listings in Quarto
text:
How It Works
1. Put each project in its own folder with an index.qmd:


Project structure

posts/
├── sql-portfolio/index.qmd
├── shopify-channel-analysis/index.qmd
├── wellness-ranch-cep/index.qmd
└── campus-video-production/index.qmd

2. Give each page metadata in its YAML header:


posts/sql-portfolio/index.qmd

---
title: "SQL & BigQuery Learning Portfolio"
description: "Three DataCamp courses documented with marketing-focused SQL examples."
date: 2026-10-23
categories: [SQL, BigQuery, GitHub Pages]
image: thumbnail.png
---

3. Add a listing block to the page where the gallery should appear:


listings.qmd

listing:
  contents: posts
  type: grid
  sort: "date desc"
  categories: true
  filter-ui: true

section: Using Listings for a Portfolio Website
text:
Using Listings for a Portfolio Website

Show your best work first with sort: "date desc" or a custom order field.
Categories become filters. Tag projects by skill (SQL, GA4, Video) so recruiters can jump to what they care about.
Thumbnails sell the project. Add an image: to each post; a chart or screenshot works great.
Low maintenance. New project = new folder. The gallery updates itself.
RSS feed option. Add feed: true to let people subscribe to new posts.

title: CEP Analytics Dashboard
text:
How It’s Built
The dashboard is a single Quarto file using format: dashboard. Rows and columns are set with headings, and each chart is an R code chunk:


cep-dashboard.qmd

---
title: "Wellness Ranch Therapy · GA4 Dashboard"
format:
  dashboard:
    orientation: rows
    theme: [cosmo, custom.scss]
---

Each # heading becomes a page (tab), ## becomes a row, and ### becomes a column:
# Acquisition                 ← page / tab
## Row {height=18%}           ← KPI value boxes
## Row {height=47%}
### Column {width=60%}        ← sessions by source chart
### Column {width=40%}        ← sessions by channel chart
KPIs use #| content: valuebox, the charts are interactive plotly graphs, and the tracking table is a DT datatable. The GA4 numbers are saved as CSV files in the data/ folder, so the dashboard re-renders with new numbers whenever the CSVs are updated.
Because it lives in the same Quarto project, it shares the site’s SCSS theme, so the branding stays consistent.

title: Styling a Quarto Website with CSS & SCSS
text:
Quarto sites look clean out of the box thanks to Bootstrap themes, but every site using the default theme looks the same. CSS and SCSS let you match your personal or client brand (colors, fonts, spacing) so the site feels like yours.






TipQuick definitions




CSS (Cascading Style Sheets): the language browsers use to style HTML (colors, fonts, layout).
SCSS (Sassy CSS): a superset of CSS that adds variables, nesting, and functions. Quarto compiles it into regular CSS when you render.

title: Styling a Quarto Website with CSS & SCSS
text:
SCSS Features Worth Knowing



Variables
Store a value once ($brand-green) and reuse it everywhere. Change it in one place to rebrand.




Nesting
Write &:hover inside .card-box instead of repeating the selector. It keeps related styles together.




Functions
lighten($brand-green, 15%) makes color variations on the fly, like the gradient in the demo box above.

title: Styling a Quarto Website with CSS & SCSS
text:
Light & Dark Mode
SCSS also makes a dark-mode toggle easy. Quarto adds the switch to the navbar automatically:


_quarto.yml

format:
  html:
    theme:
      light: [cosmo, custom.scss]
      dark:  [darkly, custom-dark.scss]

title: Styling a Quarto Website with CSS & SCSS
text:
Tips for Marketing Sites

Start with brand variables. Pull the client’s hex codes from their style guide into scss:defaults first.
Use $primary instead of hard-coding colors, so buttons and links stay consistent.
Keep custom classes reusable (.card-box, .skill) instead of styling one-off elements.
Check contrast. Brand gold on white can fail accessibility, so use it for accents and borders, not body text.
Inspect in the browser (right-click → Inspect) to find the exact selector you need to override.
